messages:
alex: thinking out loud — can we decouple probe sampling from the rollout router? instead of embedding probe logic in the edge we publish a tiny probe-exchange protocol between observer agents and the decision plane.
jenn: curious — what problem are you trying to solve specifically?
alex: current issues: regions get different probe densities, long tails when a variant fails slowly, and rollout controller has to know too much about local health. i want a flow where local agents run cheap probes and exchange summarized signals with the central decider.
oliver: sounds promising. how would fallback be triggered? immediate local fallback or central policy?
alex: hybrid. local agent can trigger a fast local escape hatch if latency/error spikes exceed a high watermark. central decider takes aggregated signals and can enact global rollback or adjust traffic slices.
li: important: we must avoid split-brain between local and central. need clear precedence and TTLs on local decisions.
jenn: +1 on TTLs. propose: local fast-fallback only for up to X seconds or until central ACKs a different decision. safety leash.
alex: exactly. sketch:
```
probe -> local aggregator -> if breach -> local fallback (reason=fast_local, ttl=30s) -> notify central
central receives summaries every 10s -> can escalate to global rollback (reason=global_safety)
```
devex: UX question — how will this surface in console? need clear indicators of which path caused fallback (local vs central) and the probe sample rate per region.
oliver: also consider canaries that are stateful: local fallback might leave sessions stranded. we should include a session-drain hint in the local fallback response, e.g., 302 route->fallback with X-drain header.
li: cryptic edge case: what if a misconfigured local agent keeps flipping fallback on/off rapidly? we should debounce and rate-limit local fallback signals and include an operator rate budget.
jenN: (typo) jenn: agree — rate budgets + cooldowns. default cooldown 60s with exponential backoff for repeated flips.
infra-bot: build-check: probe-agent v2 passed unit tests; canary-sim matrix job queued. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks infra-bot. another design detail: signal fidelity. local agents should send 2 aggregated values: (error_pct, p95_latency_ms) plus a provenance tag (sample_count, probe_version). keep payload tiny.
jenn: do we need to encode model-level compatibility? e.g., some rollouts involve quantized variants that behave differently on p95. perhaps include variant_meta.
alex: yes include variant_id and model_size tag. keep it optional.
devex: logging/observability: include a trace id in the notification so we can correlate fallback events to traces in console.
li: security: agents need mTLS and short-lived creds. central decider should verify TTL on agent identity and reject stale agents.
oliver: question: how do we test this without risking production? suggest a staging path: run central decider in "shadow mode" for a week, then enable local fast-fallback in a low-traffic region.
alex: plan sounds good. next steps: 1) RFC doc for probe exchange payload & precedence rules; 2) implement local debounce + TTL; 3) devex mock UI; 4) staged rollout in eu-west-2.
jenN: (typo) jenn: i'll take point on the RFC writeup.
infra-bot: ci-update: canary-sim matrix passed for eu-west-2 shadow run. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/run/1755 :rocket:
alex: awesome. one final thought — add a configurable safety-leash param per tenant so enterprise customers can set local-fallback=off if they require centralized control.
jenn: noted. we'll add tenant override and default to on for hosted.
devex: i'll draft console mocks showing "Local fast-fallback (30s TTL) — triggered by region eu-west-2" + drilldown.
li: i'll draft auth requirements and short-lived cert flow.
alex: thanks all. i'll start the RFC and tag you. :thumbsup:
